subject: math

objective.text: Draw a line plot for a data set. Answer questions and draw conclusions from measurement data.

explanations.title: Start with the table
explanations.text: Find the smallest and the greatest measurement in the table. The number line goes from the smallest to the greatest. Label every number between, even with no data.

explanations.title: Draw the line plot
explanations.text: Draw a number line. Label it with the unit. Put one X above the number for each measurement. Make every X the same size. Add a title.

explanations.title: Ask questions of a line plot
explanations.text: The most common measurement has the tallest stack of X's. The difference is the greatest minus the smallest. The total is the number of X's. An X far from the rest is outside the main group.

explanations.title: Table or line plot
explanations.text: A table organizes data. A line plot lets you compare the amounts at a glance.

explanations.title: Fewer than
explanations.text: To find a number that is fewer than a total, add the parts first. Then take away the amount fewer. A tape diagram helps.

examples.title: Bean plants
examples.text: Bean plant heights go from 9 to 15 cm. No plant is 10 cm, so 10 has no X. The most common height is 13 cm. The difference between tallest and shortest is 6 cm. There are 26 plants.

examples.title: Sit and reach
examples.text: Reach distances go from 22 to 34 cm. No student is 24, 32 or 33 cm, so those have no X. The most common reach is 28 cm. The difference is 12 cm.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
